description: Desarrollamos una arquitectura de navegación autónoma y propulsión de ciclo cerrado para alunizaje de precisión en terreno accidentado. Nuestro sistema integra protección térmica avanzada y el protocolo de emergencia "Maniobra Ícaro" para garantizar la supervivencia absoluta de la tripulación en el espacio profundo.
summary:
We created the Lunar Site Navigator (LLSN), an advanced aerospace engineering architecture designed specifically for human spaceflight, precision landings over rugged lunar terrain, and emergency vacuum aborts. To solve the unique problems of the Moon—such as having no atmosphere, deep crater shadows, and a dangerous 2.5 to 2.8-roundtrip communication delay with Earth—the system relies on
-Local Edge Processing & Sensor Fusion: Instead of relying on Earth, on-board flight computers use a multimodal sensor suite (optical cameras, Flash LIDAR, and radar) processed through an Extended Kalman Filter to handle real-time terrain navigation and hazard avoidance.
-A Modular Design: The vehicle splits into a non-sacrificial crew maneuver capsule and a disposable landing gear module optimized for vacuum flight.   
-High-Pressure Propulsion & The "Icarus Maneuver": It uses closed-cycle high-pressure engines for smooth descent and an automated emergency escape protocol (the "Icarus Maneuver") that executes a full-power propellant depletion burn, unpowered inertial coasting, and clean pyrotechnic stage separation to rescue the crew if anything goes wrong.   
It is vital because it establishes a non-negotiable standard of absolute human crew survival and multi-layer redundancy. By removing single points of failure in life support, computing, and structural safety, it ensures astronauts can safely land and execute emergency extractions completely independent of Earth's delayed intervention.
details: The system we propose consists of camera and proximity sensors, designd to prevent astronauts from facing the risk of lunar collision or a major accident. The proposed setup includes a flinght computer, as well as system for monitoring altitude,proximity, and speed sistems. The proyect is different from the others because it is not designed to compete with the other proyects, but rather to contribute to space exploration-driven by the team´s passion for the field. The factors the team considered included the risks involved during a lunar descent and throughout the stay on the moon.
